meta.description: Text-to-speech narration templates for a virtual soroban-style abacus. Every string is written to be read aloud: no symbols, full sentences.

placeholders.place: Rod position, 1 = units, 2 = tens, and so on (right to left).
placeholders.place_name: Spoken name of the rod, from place_names (e.g. 'tens').
placeholders.next_place: place + 1, the rod to the left.
placeholders.next_place_name: Spoken name of the next rod.
placeholders.count: How many beads are being moved.
placeholders.current_value: Full value currently shown on the abacus.
placeholders.user_answer: Answer typed or spoken by the learner.
placeholders.total_rods: Number of rods on the abacus.

usage_notes: Replace placeholders before sending text to the TTS engine.
Numbers are inserted as digits; most TTS engines read them correctly.
Each template is a single sentence or short pair of sentences so the animation can sync per step.
Where a key has 'one' and 'many' forms, use 'one' when count is 1.

glossary.abacus: An abacus is a counting tool made of rods and beads. Each bead position stands for a number.
glossary.rod: A rod is a vertical wire that holds the beads. Each rod stands for one place value, like units, tens, or hundreds.
glossary.bead: A bead is a small piece that slides on a rod. Its position tells us what number it shows.
glossary.beam: The beam is the horizontal bar in the middle. Beads touching the beam are counted. Beads away from the beam are not counted.
glossary.heaven_bead: The heaven bead sits above the beam. When it touches the beam, it is worth five.
glossary.earth_bead: The earth beads sit below the beam. Each one touching the beam is worth one. There are four on every rod.
glossary.place_value: Place value means each rod has its own worth. The rod on the right is units, the next is tens, then hundreds, and so on.
glossary.carry: A carry means we pass one to the next rod on the left, because the current rod is full.
glossary.borrow: A borrow means we take one from the next rod on the left, because the current rod does not have enough.
glossary.complement: A complement is the number that completes a target. The five complement of 3 is 2, because 3 plus 2 makes 5. The ten complement of 3 is 7, because 3 plus 7 makes 10.
glossary.five_complement: The five complement method helps when there are not enough earth beads. We use the heaven bead, worth five, and fix the difference.
glossary.ten_complement: The ten complement method helps when a rod goes past nine or runs short. We move one on the next rod, worth ten here, and fix the difference.
glossary.clear: Clearing the abacus means moving every bead away from the beam, so every rod shows zero.

earth_add.one: Move one earth bead up to the beam on the {place_name} rod.
earth_add.many: Move {count} earth beads up to the beam on the {place_name} rod.

earth_remove.one: Move one earth bead down, away from the beam, on the {place_name} rod.
earth_remove.many: Move {count} earth beads down, away from the beam, on the {place_name} rod.

bead_actions.heaven_add: Move the heaven bead down to the beam on the {place_name} rod. That adds five.
bead_actions.heaven_remove: Move the heaven bead up, away from the beam, on the {place_name} rod. That removes five.
bead_actions.heaven_and_earth_add: Move the heaven bead down, and {count} earth beads up, on the {place_name} rod.
bead_actions.heaven_and_earth_remove: Move the heaven bead up, and {count} earth beads down, on the {place_name} rod.

session.welcome: Welcome to the abacus. Let's learn together, one step at a time.
session.ready: The abacus is clear. All rods show zero.
session.enter_number: Enter the first number to set on the abacus.
session.next_digit: Now let's work on the {place_name} digit, {digit}.
session.start_from_left: We start from the leftmost digit and move right.
session.start_from_right: We start from the rightmost digit and move left.
session.result_check: Look at the beads. The abacus shows {result}.
session.cleared: All beads are away from the beam. The abacus shows zero.
session.replay_prompt: Would you like to watch that again?
session.goodbye: Great practice today. See you next time.

direct_addition.intro: This is direct addition. There is enough room on the {place_name} rod, so we simply add {number}.
direct_addition.explain: We can add {number} directly because the {place_name} rod has enough free beads.

direct_subtraction.intro: This is direct subtraction. The {place_name} rod has enough beads, so we simply take away {number}.
direct_subtraction.explain: We can subtract {number} directly because the {place_name} rod holds at least {number}.

five_complement_addition.intro: This needs the five complement. We want to add {number}, but there are not enough earth beads free.

steps.add_five: First, add five by bringing the heaven bead down on the {place_name} rod.

five_complement_addition.explain: Adding {number} is the same as adding five and taking away {complement_5}. Five minus {complement_5} is {number}.

five_complement_subtraction.intro: This needs the five complement. We want to subtract {number}, but there are not enough earth beads to remove.

steps.subtract_five: First, subtract five by lifting the heaven bead on the {place_name} rod.

five_complement_subtraction.explain: Subtracting {number} is the same as subtracting five and adding back {complement_5}. Five minus {complement_5} is {number}.

ten_complement_addition.intro: This needs the ten complement. Adding {number} to the {place_name} rod goes past nine, so we carry.

steps.carry: First, carry one. Add one on the {next_place_name} rod.

ten_complement_addition.explain: Adding {number} is the same as adding ten and taking away {complement_10}. One on the {next_place_name} rod is worth ten.
ten_complement_addition.outro: The {place_name} rod now shows {digit}, and the {next_place_name} rod has one more.

ten_complement_subtraction.intro: This needs the ten complement. The {place_name} rod has less than {number}, so we borrow.

steps.borrow: First, borrow one. Subtract one on the {next_place_name} rod.

ten_complement_subtraction.explain: Subtracting {number} is the same as subtracting ten and adding back {complement_10}. One on the {next_place_name} rod is worth ten.
ten_complement_subtraction.outro: The {place_name} rod now shows {digit}, and the {next_place_name} rod has one less.

special_cases.carry_cascade: The {next_place_name} rod is already full, so the carry moves one rod further to the left.
special_cases.borrow_cascade: The {next_place_name} rod is empty, so we borrow from the next rod on the left and pass it down.
special_cases.add_zero: Adding zero changes nothing. Move on to the next digit.
special_cases.subtract_zero: Subtracting zero changes nothing. Move on to the next digit.
special_cases.rod_zero: The {place_name} rod shows zero. No beads touch the beam.
special_cases.rod_nine: The {place_name} rod shows nine. The heaven bead and all four earth beads touch the beam.
special_cases.overflow: The answer needs more rods than this abacus has. This abacus has {total_rods} rods.
special_cases.negative_result: The answer would be below zero. This abacus works with positive numbers only.
special_cases.invalid_input: That doesn't look like a valid number. Please enter digits only.

incorrect: Not quite. Let's look at the beads again.
That's not the answer. Let's check step by step.
feedback.correct_answer_reveal: The correct answer is {result}. You answered {user_answer}.
feedback.hint_method: Hint: check whether the rod has enough beads. If not, think about the five or ten complement.
feedback.hint_place: Hint: look at the {place_name} rod first.
encouragement: Take your time. Accuracy matters more than speed.
Every mistake is a step toward learning.
You're getting better with each problem.
feedback.your_turn: Now it's your turn. Move the beads to add {number} on the {place_name} rod.

playback.slow_mode: Slow mode is on. I'll explain each step in detail.
playback.fast_mode: Fast mode is on. I'll keep it short.
